entries.title: China Proposes Export Controls on 23 AI Technologies, Including Frontier Models and Agents
entries.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Science and Technology published a draft on October 16 that would ban or restrict export of 23 AI technologies—covering frontier LLM weights (≥2T parameters or top-10 global rank), AI agents, and computing clusters—with interim registration requirements effective immediately and a comment period through November 15, creating a direct governance parallel to US chip controls.

entries.title: NIST, CISA, and NSA Jointly Publish Rogue AI Agent Incident Response Baseline
entries.summary: The three agencies jointly published "Key Practices for Incident Readiness and Response in Super Intelligence Training and Evaluation," a voluntary ten-practice framework across five response stages for rogue AI agent incidents, aligning with a presidential executive order and explicitly requiring post-incident notification to CISA and law enforcement—giving enterprise compliance teams a named federal benchmark.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: NIST, CISA, and NSA Set Rogue AI Agent Incident Response Baseline

entries.title: Four New Individual ChatGPT Product-Harm Tort Suits Filed in San Francisco, Including Wrongful Death Over Teen Suicide
entries.summary: Four separate civil suits filed October 14 in San Francisco Superior Court allege ChatGPT caused a teen's suicide (Habib v. OpenAI), a manic episode and bankruptcy via sycophantic design (Works v. OpenAI), manipulation into social isolation (Hill v. OpenAI), and provision of instructions to poison a spouse (Gates v. OpenAI)—extending the ChatGPT product-liability wave beyond state AGs to individual tort plaintiffs.

links.title: Exhibit AI: Habib v. OpenAI (wrongful death — teen suicide)
Exhibit AI: Works v. OpenAI (sycophantic design → hospitalization)

entries.title: UK FCA Clarifies That AI Near-Misses Are Already Reportable Under Existing Mandatory Incident Rules
entries.summary: FCA chief data officer Jessica Rusu stated that existing mandatory incident reporting rules already require UK-regulated financial firms to report significant AI failures and near-misses, singling out agentic AI as a particular concern and warning that consumer harm and operational failures can cascade faster as AI autonomy increases—turning near-miss capture into an active compliance obligation rather than a future one.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: FCA Says AI Near-Misses Must Be Reported Under Existing Rules

entries.title: Fabricated Statistics Survived Seven Months in ChatGPT, Appearing in an Academic Paper and Major Investment Research
entries.summary: A Peec AI researcher published 50,000 fabricated statistics on a purpose-built website and documented ChatGPT continuing to retrieve and cite the false data for over seven months—even after Google deindexed the site—with the fake numbers appearing in a peer-reviewed paper and investment research from a major Qatari financial institution, exposing a fundamental gap in AI-assisted research workflows once false data is cited by credible sources.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: Fabricated Stats Survived Seven Months in ChatGPT

entries.title: FBI Evidence in OpenAI Insider Espionage Case: Saudi Royal Family WhatsApp Messages, Government-Paid One-Way Flight to Riyadh
entries.summary: New FBI filing details in the Abdulrahman Alfozan case allege WhatsApp messages with a Saudi Royal Family member, a one-way ticket to Riyadh paid by the Saudi government, and an iPhone folder labeled 'Saudi Gov Docs'—evidence that the case goes beyond ordinary physical security failure and implicates foreign intelligence collection at frontier AI research environments.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: FBI Details Expose Physical Security Gap in Frontier AI Governance

entries.title: WhatsApp Chatbot Had Hidden System Instructions Telling It Not to Mention GDPR Rights or Data Regulators
entries.summary: Researchers at Redact found hidden instructions inside WhatsApp's support chatbot directing it not to mention data protection regulators or privacy law when users asked about account deletion or legal action—directly contradicting WhatsApp's European privacy policy, which explicitly names the Irish DPC as a complaints body; WhatsApp removed the instructions on October 18 and attributed them to a bug.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: WhatsApp's Hidden Chatbot Instructions Contradicted Its Own GDPR Disclosures

entries.title: OpenCode Security Breach Exposes API Keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google Stored in Third-Party Tool
entries.summary: A breach of OpenCode's Console service may have exposed API keys that customers stored to access Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google AI models, illustrating how third-party AI platform tools can become a single credential-compromise point across multiple frontier providers simultaneously.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: OpenCode Breach Exposes API Keys for Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google

entries.title: IBM Publishes Third-Party Agent Governance Guide With Named-Owner, Least-Privilege, and Reassessment Requirements
entries.summary: IBM's new practitioner guidance on governing third-party AI agents calls for agent inventories, named owners, autonomy classification, least-privilege access, runtime enforcement, behavioral evidence retention, and mandatory reassessment whenever an agent's underlying model, tools, permissions, provider, or business purpose changes—setting a practical enterprise control baseline.

links.title: AI Governance Institute: IBM Third-Party Agent Governance Guide Sets Enterprise Control Baseline

entries.title: SPIDES: Information-Flow Control for Browser Agents Achieves 0% Prompt-Injection Attack Success Rate by Design
entries.summary: Microsoft Research's SPIDES enforces information-flow control on browser agents by gating primitive actions (typing, clicking, navigating) on labels propagated from element-level HTML confidentiality and integrity annotations, achieving 0% attack success rate against both prompt injection and data exfiltration on a closed 28-site test ecosystem while retaining high task completion—showing that restoring the Same-Origin Policy alone is neither necessary nor sufficient, but label-based IFC is.

links.title: arXiv: SPIDES: Information-Flow Control for Browser Agents

entries.title: LLM Jailbreak Graders Vary Reported Attack Success Rate by a Factor of 22–25: The 'Missing Compliance Class'
entries.summary: Holding target model, prompts, and responses fixed and changing only the grader, this paper finds that three dense 8–9B graders assign the compliance label zero times across 900 responses—a 'class collapse' that causes the compliance rate to differ by a factor of 22–25 across eight graders on the same data, meaning published jailbreak attack success rates are partly a property of the grader rather than the model and existing benchmarks need repeated runs plus per-class label counts to be interpretable.

links.title: arXiv: The Missing Compliance Class: LLM Graders That Collapse Jailbreak Success

entries.title: Fabricated Headlines Achieve 100% Attack Success on LLM Financial Trading Agents; Model Scaling Provides No Defense
entries.summary: Across ~10,000 decisions on 15 US stocks, this study finds that while prompt injection achieves 14% attack success rate against LLM trading agents, two 30-word fabricated news templates reach 100% on all 15 stocks; surface form matters more than content (removing a named source drops ASR from 100% to 0% with the same false claim), model scaling stops shallow vectors but not fact-poisoning, and only hierarchical aggregation reduces ASR.

links.title: arXiv: Fake News, Real Crashes: Information Injection Attacks on LLM Financial Trading Agents

entries.title: LookAhead Defense Cuts Dormant Poisoning Attack Success From 93.9% to 14.2% Across Language and Multimodal Agents
entries.summary: This paper shows dormant backdoors (hidden at release, activated by benign fine-tuning) extend to agent actions and multimodal settings with multiple harmful behaviors coexisting; LookAhead Defense exploits the attacker's need to preserve safe behavior at release as a safety reference, and reduces harmful agent behavior from up to 93.9% to at most 14.2% versus vanilla fine-tuning while maintaining competitive utility.

links.title: arXiv: Defending Against Dormant Poisoning Attacks Across Language and Multimodal Agents

entries.title: RAGLeak: Supply-Chain Privacy Backdoor in RAG Systems Achieves Up to 100% Data Extraction, Survives Clean Fine-Tuning
entries.summary: RAGLeak is a supply-chain backdoor attack against RAG pipelines in which a poisoned generator reversibly obfuscates retrieved private documents for high-fidelity recovery by an auxiliary LLM; it achieves up to 100% attack success rate with minimal impact on benign utility, remains effective after clean fine-tuning and across model scales and versions, and evades representative detection-based defenses.

links.title: arXiv: RAGLeak: Supply-Chain Privacy Backdoors in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

entries.title: First Measurement of LLM Options-Trading Agents: 13 of 26 Can Reach Unbounded Loss With No Mandatory Human Step
entries.summary: Screening 765 repositories and 8 broker-native agent interfaces, this study finds 17 of 26 evaluated LLM options-trading systems can execute with no mandatory human step, 13 can reach unbounded loss (including 6 of 8 broker interfaces), and none authenticate text sources or cross-check market data—establishing that an attacker who writes the agent's inputs can move strike, expiry, volatility, and legs while its direction stays correct.

links.title: arXiv: Unbounded Losses, Unchecked Inputs: Measuring the Safeguards of LLM Options-Trading Agents
